Cybersecurity threats are evolving rapidly as attackers increasingly leverage AI, blockchain infrastructure, and sophisticated social engineering to exploit familiar vulnerabilities across enterprise and industrial systems.

### Key Points
- ReliaQuest confirmed a social engineering attack where hackers used a lookalike domain and fake SSO page to harvest credentials.
- A new Android fraud bot named Octagon is being sold as malware-as-a-service for $1,400 per month, targeting banking and crypto apps.
- The ToxNetV2 botnet has integrated NVIDIA NIM’s large language models to automate and optimize its malicious operational workflows.
- CISA reported that Iranian threat actors targeted over 100 internet-exposed U.S. water systems by exploiting programmable logic controllers.
- Microsoft warned that the window for patching vulnerabilities is shrinking as attackers use AI to accelerate the exploitation of newly disclosed flaws.
- A supply chain attack dubbed Deadbugz is distributing malicious Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to steal sensitive credentials from AI agents.

### Why it Matters
The rapid integration of AI and decentralized infrastructure into malware campaigns is significantly shortening the time between vulnerability disclosure and active exploitation. Organizations face heightened risk as traditional security perimeters struggle to keep pace with automated, AI-assisted threats that bypass standard detection methods.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says AI data centers can fix the very grid they’re straining
articles.author: Brent D. Griffiths
articles.content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the AI industry needs to do "better" when it comes to data centers.
"The technology industry, the builders, and, have to do a much better job working with the communities to get prepared for this AI infrastructure build-out," Huang told CNBC's Jim Cramer on Wednesday when asked about how Nvidia's customers could show communities they are serious about data center concerns.
Huang is the latest voice in tech, and arguably the biggest so far, to acknowledge that the industry has to do a better job of selling communities on building data centers. Polling shows that Americans have become deeply skeptical of the massive facilities that house the advanced chips that train and serve AI demand.
Huang said the industry needs to sell the idea that data center construction can help reindustrialize the nation. Addressing a frequent concern, Huang said data centers could actually lower energy costs.
"It is also the case this is the first time in probably the last century that we're able to invest in sustainable energy, invest in improving our energy grid, securing our energy supply, reducing the cost of energy across the country," he said. "This is the first time in history that we're able to do that because of the enormous market dynamics, the market forces that are able to invest in the energy ecosystem."
Business Insider has previously reported that rapid data center expansion could increase electricity costs. A recent study by researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology found that data centers could reduce consumer costs by adjusting their power consumption.
The MIT researchers found that data centers that shift their power consumption to off-peak hours could lower average energy costs by up to 4% in the Mid-Atlantic, 5% in Texas, and 2% in 11 western states compared to facilities that didn't change their consumption patterns. The researchers studied power grids in each of those three areas due to the prevalence of data centers there.
There is a big caveat to their findings. The researchers said that under some scenarios, data centers would need to shift nearly 50% of their energy consumption to non-peak hours, such as the afternoon.
On Wednesday, Nvidia reported that data center revenue totaled $89 billion in the second quarter of FY 26, up 117% from a year ago. The figure also surpassed Wall Street's estimates, illustrating just how lucrative the broader AI buildout is for the world's largest company by market cap.
Like President Donald Trump, Huang warned of the costs to the US if data centers aren't built out.
"We have to make sure that our communities, our society, all of our companies, all of our people in the United States embrace this technology so that we can take advantage of what this technology could do for all of our ecosystems, all of our economy, and all of our societies," Huang said. He added, "Otherwise, we're going to get left behind."
At the same time, the vibes in the US look increasingly dour. Governors have moved to pump the brakes on data center construction amid a growing public backlash.
Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who is seeking reelection, imposed an effective moratorium on new data center construction until state agencies complete a comprehensive audit. Abbott was rather blunt about how he went from declaring Texas the "epicenter of AI development" to imposing a moratorium in less than a year.
"They basically dug their own grave for the problem that's been caused for them, and that's why they got the backlash they deserve," Abbott said during an interview on ABC's "This Week."
articles.summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urged the technology industry to improve community engagement regarding data center construction to address public skepticism and support national reindustrialization and energy grid modernization.

### Key Points
- Nvidia reported $89 billion in second-quarter data center revenue, marking a 117% increase compared to the previous year.
- Jensen Huang argued that data centers could lower national energy costs by investing in sustainable infrastructure and grid improvements.
- MIT research suggests data centers could reduce consumer energy costs by up to 5% if facilities shift power consumption to off-peak hours.
- Texas Governor Greg Abbott recently imposed a moratorium on new data center construction following public backlash over energy demands.
- Huang warned that failing to embrace AI infrastructure could cause the United States to fall behind in global economic and technological competition.

### Why it Matters
The tension between rapid AI infrastructure growth and local energy concerns highlights a critical bottleneck for the technology sector's expansion. Successfully balancing these massive power requirements with community needs is essential to maintaining the momentum of the current AI boom and preventing further regulatory pushback.

articles.title: Nvidia Soars 7% In Premarket As It Leads Upswing In Chip Stocks After Strong Earnings
articles.author:
Siladitya Ray, Forbes Staff, 
 Siladitya Ray, Forbes Staff
 https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/
articles.content:
Topline
Nvidia’s stock price soared in premarket trading early on Thursday, reversing a more than week-long slump, and triggered an upswing in other chip stocks after the company's forecast of a 70% jump in revenue next fiscal year appeared to tamp down on market anxiety about a potential slowdown in demand for AI compute.
Key Facts
In premarket trading early on Thursday, Nvidia’s stock price rose to $224.83 per share, up more than 7.2% from Wednesday’s close.
The post-earnings boost wiped out a slump that began last week amid anxiety over its earnings and criticism of its apparent “circular financing” deal with top AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic.
Optimism about continued AI-fueled growth boosted other top chip companies as well, with Intel’s stock rising 3.55% to $91.27, Broadcom climbing 1.8% to $362.12, while AMD’s shares rose 1.6% to $488.72 in the premarket.
Memory chipmaker Micron’s shares rose more than 4% to $976.71 as Nvidia’s earnings call acknowledged a scarcity of memory chips due to high demand from AI chipmakers.
The chip stock surge boosted the tech-heavy Nasdaq Futures index, which rose 1.10% to 29,622.25 points, while the benchmark S&P 500 futures climbed around 0.5% to 7,727.00 points.
Asian semiconductor stocks also saw a boost, with SK Hynix, Samsung and Kioxia shares rising 2.5%, 1.7% and 5% respectively.
What Do We Know About Nvidia’s Q2 Earnings?
Nvidia reported its earnings for the second quarter of 2026 on Wednesday. The company reported $96.2 billion in revenue for the second quarter, up 106% from the previous year, beating Wall Street's forecasts of $92.2 billion. Net income rose to $59.7 billion from $26.4 billion last year, and the company projected $108 billion in revenue for the current quarter—again beating analyst expectations of around $104.2 billion.
What Did The Chipmaker Say In Its Earnings Call?
In its earnings call, the company said it expects a 70% jump in sales in the next fiscal year. The company’s billionaire CEO, Jensen Huang, suggested that the 70% projection was conservative and largely due to supply chain constraints. He said: “Even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%. We are going to continue to work with our supply chain to increase on that.”

articles.summary:
Nvidia shares surged over 7% in premarket trading after the company reported strong quarterly earnings and projected a 70% revenue increase for the upcoming fiscal year.

### Key Points
- Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in second-quarter revenue, marking a 106% year-over-year increase that exceeded Wall Street expectations.
- CEO Jensen Huang stated that the projected 70% sales growth is limited by supply chain constraints rather than a lack of market demand.
- The positive earnings report triggered gains for other chipmakers, including Intel, Broadcom, AMD, and Micron.
- Asian semiconductor manufacturers, such as SK Hynix, Samsung, and Kioxia, also saw share prices rise following the announcement.
- Nasdaq Futures and S&P 500 futures climbed as investor anxiety regarding a potential slowdown in AI compute demand subsided.

### Why it Matters
Nvidia’s performance serves as a critical bellwether for the broader artificial intelligence sector and global semiconductor market. The company's ability to maintain high growth rates helps stabilize investor confidence in the long-term viability of AI infrastructure spending.

articles.title: Humanity Needs an AI Nonproliferation Treaty
articles.author: Rogé Karma
articles.content:
Sign up for Work in Progress, a newsletter where Rogé Karma investigates the mysteries of a complicated economy.
America’s biggest AI companies have spent the past few years churning out advanced new models as fast as they possibly can. Now the industry is screaming out with a nearly unified voice: Please, for the love of God, make us slow down.
In July, more than 1,300 employees from leading AI firms, including several top executives at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta, signed an open letter warning that AI capabilities could soon accelerate “beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems.” The letter urges the U.S. government to “develop the technical and governance tools” necessary to “deliberately pace” AI progress. In a comment accompanying the open letter, Shengjia Zhao, the chief scientist at Meta’s Superintelligence Labs, wrote that AI is on the cusp of creating “unprecedented social and safety risks.” Matthew Rahtz, an engineer at Google, warned that coordination was necessary to “avoid catastrophic harms.” And Leo Gao, an OpenAI researcher, compared the current pace of AI progress to “a runaway nuclear chain reaction.” Plenty of others in the industry have warned that we’ve already crossed a threshold from which there is no turning back. They worry that the most dystopian fears of an AI future—chatbot-generated bioweapons, major hacking attacks on banks or governments, rogue AI agents wreaking havoc on society—could soon become regular occurrences.
Meanwhile, the public backlash against AI data centers is growing louder by the day. But a data-center moratorium, the leading political proposal on offer, is totally mismatched to the actual problem of runaway AI development. So is the notion that AI companies can be trusted to pause their own models before things get out of hand. These companies will never unilaterally disarm. Neither, for that matter, will the countries where they’re based. The only way to truly slow things down might be to take the nuclear-reaction analogy seriously. What humanity needs is an international AI nonproliferation treaty.
For decades, technology experts have warned that AI systems will eventually become so powerful as to be dangerous. In just the past few months, “eventually” has begun to look a lot more like “now.” AI systems can already hack seemingly secure systems, invent new viruses, create hyperrealistic deepfakes, and even outsmart the humans who built them. This summer, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta each separately reported that some of their AI agents had broken out of testing environments, gone onto the open internet, and hacked into other companies’ databases. During a cybersecurity test conducted by the U.K. government in July, several AI agents engaged in what the testers called “sustained, unsanctioned activity” targeting “real people and organisations.” This included creating fake identities and sending phishing emails in order to get humans to accept malicious pieces of code.
If industry insiders are to be believed, this is just a small preview of what’s coming. Companies are entrusting more and more model development to their existing AI, creating a feedback loop that they expect to accelerate progress even further. If that happens, many experts believe, then the kind of leaps that currently occur every several months—such as the one that produced Mythos, the Anthropic model with superhacking skills—could begin happening every few weeks or days. “That world can get very scary very fast,” Garrison Lovely, the author of a forthcoming book on how to slow down AI progress, told me. “Our institutions are already struggling to keep up with the current pace of progress. Any faster and they could start to break.”
Such concerns explain why AI leaders promise every so often to self-regulate. In April, Anthropic chose to delay the public release of Mythos after realizing that the model could discover vulnerabilities in the world’s most secure IT systems. Last week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced that the company had temporarily paused some of its frontier AI development “to ensure that we can meet the appropriate alignment, security and monitoring standards for the new level of capabilities in front of us.” (It is impossible to know how serious OpenAI is given the lack of transparency into the company’s data.) But these companies are locked in a hypercompetitive race to deliver for their investors. Expecting them to cede ground to the competition for any meaningful amount of time would be naive. In 2023, Anthropic pledged to pause its frontier AI development if it couldn’t guarantee that its safety measures were adequate; earlier this year, the company walked back that commitment, arguing that a unilateral slowdown wouldn’t accomplish much if its competitors didn’t agree to do the same. Google and Meta have done the same. Clearly, government policy is needed to overcome the industry’s collective-action problem.
Unfortunately, the main form of AI-related legislation being proposed at the moment would not get the job done. State-level data-center moratoriums, such as those enacted recently in New York and Texas, might slow down AI companies a little bit by disrupting their construction plans, but they will eventually find other places to build. Even if Congress decided to pass a federal ban, AI companies could just set up data centers in other countries.
A solution favored by many Democrats in Congress, and some Republicans, is to pass legislation imposing comprehensive regulation of the AI industry, which might include mandatory safety tests or requirements that companies develop a “kill switch” to shut down models that get out of hand. That might work if the only danger came from American companies. It isn’t. According to most estimates, China’s leading AI companies are only a few months behind their American counterparts. If the U.S. were to throttle its own industry, then Chinese companies would eventually surpass them. The world would still face the dangers of fast AI progress, and America’s main geopolitical rival would control the world’s most powerful new technology.
This leaves only one way to actually slow down AI development before catastrophe strikes: a deal with China. In a recently published report, researchers at the AI Futures Project, a nonprofit dedicated to AI forecasting, walk through several different scenarios of global AI development between now and 2040, based on interviews with employees at AI companies, policy makers and wonks, and national-security experts. The only two scenarios in which the world successfully avoids “AI-driven existential catastrophe” involve agreements between the U.S. and China. “We spent a lot of time thinking through all the possible ways this could play out,” Thomas Larsen, the lead author of the project, told me. “And it is just really hard to envision a meaningful slowdown that doesn’t involve some kind of U.S.-China deal.” The open letter from the AI industry asking for a government-led deceleration effort also encourages the U.S. to pursue an “international effort.”
The key would be figuring out a system that could be set up fairly quickly, and in which both sides are confident that the other won’t cheat. Here’s where one of AI’s greatest liabilities—the fact that training new models requires huge numbers of advanced computer chips developed by a handful of companies packed into giant data centers—comes in handy. The U.S. and China could set limits on how many chips a company can use to train new models, which would mechanically force them to slow down. (Companies would still be able to use existing models to serve their customers.) Because the relevant infrastructure is physical, those limits could be enforced through a combination of on-site data-center inspections, close tracking of advanced chip sales, and, eventually, devices that monitor what a given chip is being used for. This would buy the two sides time to negotiate a more comprehensive set of guardrails and develop the verification technologies needed to enforce them. “In order to make a deal like this work, it really helps to have these very specific physical choke points that can be easily monitored,” Peter Wildeford, the head of policy at the AI Policy Network, told me. “Chips and data centers could play the role for an AI agreement that uranium and enrichment sites played for nuclear-arms agreements during the Cold War.”
Just because a deal is technically feasible doesn’t mean it’s politically possible. Scott Singer, the co-director of the China AI Initiative at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, told me that Beijing would likely see any such effort as an attempt by the West to throttle its economic development. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has shown less than zero interest in restricting the ambitions of the American AI sector. The China hawks and Silicon Valley libertarians within the MAGA coalition seem to agree that the U.S. should be keeping as far ahead of China as possible.
But the political dynamic in both countries could shift. At last month’s World AI Conference in Shanghai, Chinese President Xi Jinping ended his speech by striking a more worried tone on the subject than he previously had. He noted that AI is “advancing at a staggering speed” and that government oversight might be needed to “forestall loss of control.” A recent op-ed in a major state-owned newspaper argued that the U.S. and China should follow the model of nuclear-arms control during the Cold War to cooperate on AI safety. “The thing Beijing cares about more than just about anything is control,” Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution who specializes in Chinese technological development, told me. “So the more they come to see AI as a threat to that control, the more open they could be to some kind of agreement.”
In the U.S., the politics are even more up for grabs. The Trump administration, which has generally resisted AI regulation, has recently taken actions to prevent certain models from being released due to national-security concerns. It has also floated the more dramatic idea of using executive authority to force companies to hand over their AI models to the government. Meanwhile, according to the latest polling, 75 percent of Americans, including the majority of Republicans, oppose data centers being built near them. More than 500 localities across the country have either restricted or banned them. Could this energy be channeled into a more sweeping—and more effective—framework for AI regulation? So far, the data-center backlash has mostly focused on local environmental concerns, not great-power diplomacy. But then again, that’s exactly how the anti-nuclear movement began.

articles.title: Adobe Brings ACR’s Powerful Non-Destructive Exposure Tools Into Photoshop Itself
articles.author: Jeremy Gray
articles.content:
Adobe says that the best creative software lets users focus more on their creative ideas and less on the actual tools required to bring them to life. The company believes Photoshop’s latest update builds upon this vision and gives photographers more flexibility and choice in how they create.
These latest Photoshop innovations promise more efficiency and precision in how they edit images inside of Photoshop. Photoshop is getting a Light Adjustment Layer, a Firefly-powered masking and editing tools, and markup tools. The longtime image editing app is also getting a full-fledged AI Assisted Editor, albeit just in beta at first.
The new Light Adjustment Layer promises professional-grade lighting controls, including over Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, and Blacks. This non-destructive adjustment layer takes some of Adobe Camera Raw’s most powerful photo editing tools and puts them directly inside Photoshop. The more that photographers can do directly inside Photoshop, the better.
Powered by Firefly Image 5, the new Instruct Edit with Masks function promises to understand the entire context of a photograph. Users essentially describe what they want to change in the image, such as opening a person’s closed eyes or changing a model’s clothing, and Instruct Edit with Masks will automatically mask and change the relevant area, leaving the rest of the photo untouched.
Many photographers who work with clients or editors use Photoshop. Dedicated AI Markup tools are now available in Photoshop, letting photographers (or clients) communicate desired edits directly on the photo. Users can select areas to recolor, sketch arrows to indicate where to make changes, or draw rough sketches to suggest more significant changes to an image. Firefly then does its best to show what the markup refers to.
Although not quite as exciting for photographers as the new Light Adjustment Layer, Photoshop’s Dynamic Text can now work alongside any custom shape or path. There’s also improved Adobe Stock Panel Integration that brings more than 900 million Adobe Stock assets into Photoshop on a dockable panel, so users no longer need to leave Photoshop to discover, preview, or use Adobe Stock assets in their work.
Arriving in Photoshop today as a beta, the new AI Assisted Editor introduces a dedicated interface with a natural language bar that lets people make edits through simple prompts. Depending on the prompt, Photoshop will leverage its wide array of tools to try and achieve the desired results.
The AI Assisted Editor can work alongside AI-powered features like Remove Background, Generative Expand, Generative Fill, and Generative Upscale without requiring the user to actually do anything more than type out a few words.
“Whether you prefer prompts, precision tools, or a combination of both, Photoshop offers the flexibility to support the way you create,” Adobe says.
The new Adobe Photoshop updates are available now.

Adobe has released a significant update for Photoshop, introducing AI-powered editing tools, advanced lighting controls, and a new beta interface designed to streamline professional image manipulation workflows.

### Key Points
- The new Light Adjustment Layer integrates professional-grade controls for exposure, contrast, and shadows directly into the Photoshop workspace.
- Powered by Firefly Image 5, the Instruct Edit with Masks feature allows users to modify specific image areas using natural language descriptions.

These updates represent a strategic shift toward integrating generative AI directly into professional creative workflows to reduce manual editing time. By lowering the technical barrier for complex adjustments, Adobe aims to keep Photoshop competitive as the industry standard for photographers and digital designers.

articles.title: Android 17 boosts network security by hiding domain names, lets carriers disable 2G
articles.author: Abner Li
articles.content:
Google is out with a blog post today recapping new network security measures in Android 17.
Even with HTTPS connections, the domain names of websites (including apps) are “still visible to network operators and eavesdroppers.”
This unencrypted data can be used to build user profiles or, in the hands of malicious actors, leveraged for targeted phishing and scam campaigns.
Android 17 aims to resolve this with Encrypted Client Hello (ECH). Working with private DNS, this new privacy standard will “obscure the domain names you visit.” This works by hiding the “domain name using a secret encryption key that only the destination website can unscramble.”
By encrypting the destination website name from the very start, ECH helps ensure that, for supported websites and apps, network providers and network snoopers can no longer easily see which websites or apps you are accessing.
With OS support now available, app developers have to upgrade to OkHttp 5.5.0 and enable ECH.
Domain name data leaks in two places, (1) the initial DNS lookup and (2) the unencrypted ClientHello in the Transport Layer Security (TLS) handshake. Recent progress with the rollout of encrypted DNS and the launch of support for Encrypted ClientHello on Android 17 are helping to make online activity more private
On the network front, Android 17 allows mobile carriers to turn off 2G connectivity by default for their users. (Android 12 first introduced this user setting.) This is intended to counter SMS blaster attacks that “force nearby smartphones to drop their LTE or 5G connections and downgrade to less secure, legacy 2G networks.” Phishing texts are then sent to devices.
Meanwhile, Android 17 enforces Local Network Protection wherein apps must now request permission “before they can scan or connect to other devices on your local network.”
For everyday tasks like casting a video to your TV, developers should adopt a secure system tool, which allows you to select your TV without the app ever needing permission to see the other devices in your home.
Finally, Certificate Transparency requires “all certificates to be logged in a public registry, making such an attack much less likely to go unnoticed.”
When you connect to a secure app or website, your device verifies a certificate to confirm the site is authentic. However, if a certificate issuer is compromised, hackers could potentially create fake certificates to intercept your traffic and cause harm.
articles.summary:
Google has introduced enhanced network security features in Android 17, including Encrypted Client Hello support and stricter local network permissions to better protect user privacy and prevent malicious attacks.

### Key Points
- Android 17 implements Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) to hide domain names from network operators and eavesdroppers during the initial connection handshake.
- App developers must upgrade to OkHttp 5.5.0 and enable ECH to ensure destination website names remain encrypted and private.
- Mobile carriers can now disable 2G connectivity by default to prevent SMS blaster attacks that force devices onto insecure legacy networks.
- New local network protection requires apps to request explicit user permission before scanning or connecting to other devices on a home network.
- Certificate Transparency requirements now mandate that all security certificates be logged in a public registry to detect and prevent the use of fraudulent credentials.

### Why it Matters
These updates significantly reduce the risk of targeted phishing, data profiling, and unauthorized device tracking by closing long-standing gaps in network communication. By standardizing these security protocols, Google is forcing a shift toward a more private mobile ecosystem that limits the ability of malicious actors to intercept or manipulate user traffic.

articles.title: SEC’s Crypto Custody Shake-Up: Why the Next Bitcoin Boom Could Start on Wall Street
articles.author: Yuri Molchan
articles.content:
Wall Street may be at the threshold of a crypto custody paradigm shift. The SEC is seeking more favorable rules for digital assets, banks, advisers, and brokers. Easier custody would remove one of the key barriers for institutional Bitcoin ownership.
SEC’s Crypto Custody Shake-Up: What Changed in August 2026?
Why the SEC Is Reopening the Crypto Custody Debate
The SEC seeks regulations better suited to digital assets and blockchain settlement versus traditional custodians and securities.
The New Custody Proposal Has Reached the White House for Review
The new initiative moved into White House regulatory review in August 2026. It represents a chance for a formal SEC crypto custody proposal to emerge.
Read more: Trump Pushes CLARITY Act as Bitcoin Surges: Is Crypto Finally Getting the Rules It Needs?
How the 2026 Initiative Differs From the Failed Gensler-Era Approach
The failed approach featured tighter restrictions and limited crypto custody pathways. The 2026 initiative better reflects modern-day institutional adoption and flexibility.
What Is Crypto Custody and Why Does the SEC Care?
How Crypto Custody Works for Institutional Investors
Institutional investors typically utilize specialized third-party custodians rather than private keys. These firms secure assets, execute movements, and ensure compliance reporting.
Who Controls the Private Keys?
Private keys control transfers of Bitcoin and other digital assets. Custodians safeguard cryptographic access through cold storage, multi-signature, multi-party computation or other mechanisms.
Qualified Custodians vs. Crypto-Native Custody Providers
Qualified custodians typically consist of banks and broker dealers. Crypto-native custody providers often possess deeper technical knowledge and specialized custody tech.
Why Custody Rules Matter for Investor Protection
Crypto custody rules help prevent theft, misappropriation, and insolvency. Secure segregation of customer assets also protects against failure of a particular custodian.
From SAB 121 to SAB 122: How the SEC Removed a Major Barrier to Crypto Custody
Why SAB 121 Made Bitcoin Custody Too Expensive for Banks
SAB 121 imposed accounting burdens on banks and other entities holding crypto assets. Balance sheet costs and capital requirements were significant for custodians.
SAB 122 and the Return of Traditional Financial Institutions
SAB 122 decoupled the SAB 121 approach for crypto assets. It eliminated a key institutional barrier for banks and other traditional financial firms.
Could Banks Finally Become Major Bitcoin Custodians?
Banks already serve institutional investors and possess existing compliance infrastructure. Easier SEC crypto rules would render Bitcoin custodianship commercially viable.
The SEC’s New Crypto Custody Rules Could Open the Door to Wall Street
Why Asset Managers Need Regulated Crypto Custody
Asset managers require secure assets, audits, reporting, and regulatory responsibility. Regulated custody facilitates internal approval for large investment funds.
How Easier Custody Could Accelerate Institutional Bitcoin Adoption
Lowered custody hurdles may alleviate concerns for investment committees. Greater choice among Bitcoin custodians may also reduce concentration risk and lower fees.
Related: Senate Crypto Bill Under Fire: How Banking Lobbyists Are Fighting the CLARITY Act
The Role of Banks, Broker-Dealers and Asset Managers
Banks can safeguard assets, brokers can provide custody-trading linkage, and managers can design institutional products. The triad can provide institutional market infrastructure.
Could More Institutions Move Bitcoin From Exchanges Into Long-Term Custody?
Large investors often seek segregated custody versus permanent exchange exposure. Greater option sets will encourage more Bitcoin into institutional custody.
SEC Rule 15c3-3 and Crypto: A Separate Custody Problem
How the Customer Protection Rule Applies to Crypto Asset Securities
Rule 15c3-3 mandates possession, control, reserve, or safeguarding of customer securities. Crypto asset securities, therefore, fall under similar obligations.
Why Crypto Asset Securities Are Different From Bitcoin
Bitcoin typically falls outside the scope of securities-specific custody rules. Crypto asset securities face additional regulatory obligations versus Bitcoin.
What the SEC’s 2025 Guidance Changed for Broker-Dealers
The SEC provided more practical guidance for control of crypto asset securities. This was a policy pivot versus the special-purpose broker-dealer model of the past.
H3: The Remaining Regulatory Gaps for Crypto Broker-Dealers
Wallet controls, insolvency, record-keeping, and mixed crypto business lines remain areas of concern. Future SEC crypto custody rules should seek to address them.
| Area | Previous Situation | What Could Change | Potential Impact on Bitcoin | 
|---|---|---|---|
| SEC Crypto Custody Rules | Unclear and restrictive custody framework | Broader, more flexible rules | Easier institutional access | 
| SAB 121 / SAB 122 | High accounting burden for banks | Lower balance-sheet pressure | More banks may offer Bitcoin custody | 
| Qualified Custodians | Limited number of viable providers | Banks and crypto-native firms could compete | Lower fees and less concentration risk | 
| Bitcoin ETF Custody | Heavy reliance on specialized crypto custodians | Traditional banks could enter the market | Stronger ETF infrastructure | 
| Rule 15c3-3 Crypto | Complex treatment for crypto asset securities | Clearer broker-dealer custody standards | Better institutional market access | 
| Institutional Bitcoin Custody | Operational and regulatory barriers | More regulated custody options | Larger Bitcoin allocations become easier | 
| Tokenized Securities | Limited institutional infrastructure | Custody rules could support tokenized assets | Broader digital asset adoption | 
| Main Risk | Regulatory uncertainty | Rules may still change or face legal challenges | Bullish impact remains uncertain | 
Why the SEC’s New Approach Could Be More Crypto-Friendly
Moving Away From the Special Purpose Broker-Dealer Model
The special purpose model was limiting both crypto securities and wider adoption. Broader institutional participation would become possible under a more flexible framework.
Why the Old Framework Was Considered Unworkable
Compliance costs limited the commercial viability of the special purpose model. Brokers and others viewed it as inflexible and unprofitable.
A More Flexible Approach to Qualified Custodians
A modern qualified custodian approach could feature more custody variations. Multiple types of banks, brokers, and crypto-native firms could compete for institutional business.
Self-Custody, Third-Party Custody and Institutional Safeguarding
While self-custody grants more control, institutional investors may favor third-party alternatives. Hybrid approaches could provide an alternative for institutional investors.
Bitcoin ETFs Changed the Custody Equation
Why Spot Bitcoin ETFs Need Institutional-Grade Custody
Spot Bitcoin ETFs involve large Bitcoin balances on behalf of investors. Issuers, therefore, require higher security, verification, and transaction controls.
ETF Inflows Are Creating New Demand for Bitcoin Custodians
Every large ETF inflow represents greater Bitcoin requiring institutional custody. Asset size and volume will drive greater demand for institutional Bitcoin custody.
From Coinbase to Banks: Who Will Control Institutional Bitcoin?
Crypto-native firms dominate the current institutional custody landscape. However, banks represent a potential disruptor through trusted relationships and distribution.
Could Lower Custody Friction Drive the Next Wave of ETF Demand?
Eased competition may lower fees and improve ETF economics. Familiar banking relationships and easier approvals could also accelerate adoption.
The Trillion-Dollar Opportunity Behind Crypto Custody
How Much Institutional Capital Could Enter Crypto?
Global institutional capital under management totals trillions of dollars. Even small Bitcoin allocations could represent significant demand.
Read more: Congress Crypto Bill Delay: CLARITY Act Vote Pushed to September as 2026 Passage Hopes Fade
Why Custody Is a Bottleneck for Trillions in Assets
Large institutional investors cannot ignore fiduciary, audit, and compliance implications. Weaknesses in custody can, therefore, represent a barrier for institutional investment.
Tokenized Securities Could Expand the Market Beyond Bitcoin
Tokenized bonds, funds and equities also need custody infrastructure. Such demand could expand institutional custody market opportunity beyond just Bitcoin.
The Convergence of Crypto, ETFs and Traditional Securities
Bitcoin ETFs already represent a convergence between crypto and traditional securities. Tokenization could accelerate deeper integration with conventional capital markets.
SEC Crypto Custody vs. the Clarity Act: Which Matters More for Bitcoin?
Regulatory Clarity Is Becoming a Competitive Advantage
Institutions favor regulatory certainty as it reduces costs and risk. Clarity also helps attract capital and product development versus regulatory uncertainty.
What Happens If Congress Delays Comprehensive Crypto Legislation?
Agencies can act under existing rules while legislation is pending. SEC and CFTC policy decisions, therefore, can shape markets even before congressional action.
Why SEC and CFTC Rules Could Shape Crypto Before Congress Acts
Both agencies have rulemaking authorities that can impact custody, trading and disclosures. Markets and companies often respond to such moves before congressional action.
Could Regulatory Fragmentation Still Slow Institutional Adoption?
Fragmented requirements across the SEC, the CFTC, banks and states can raise costs. It may also create uncertainty regarding appropriate compliance approaches.
Who Could Benefit Most From the SEC’s Crypto Custody Changes?
Coinbase and Crypto-Native Custodians
Crypto-native custodians may benefit from greater institutional demand. However, they also face increased competition from banks and other parties.
Banks and Traditional Custody Giants
Banks can already safeguard enormous sums of traditional assets. Easier crypto rules represent an opportunity to add Bitcoin and other digital assets.
Bitcoin ETF Issuers and Asset Managers
More custody options can reduce concentration risk and improve their negotiating position. Asset managers may find more flexibility in new product launches.
Institutional Investors and Family Offices
Institutional capital and family offices could benefit from safer and more familiar custody options for their Bitcoin allocations.
Tokenization Platforms and Digital Securities Markets
Institutions require secure custody alongside issuance, trading, and settlement. Better custody rules can facilitate broader adoption of digital securities.
Could Easier Crypto Custody Trigger the Next Bitcoin Boom?
The Institutional Adoption Flywheel
More custody options will attract more capital, which will spur product innovation and greater Bitcoin demand.
H3: More Custody Options → More Capital → More Bitcoin Demand
A variety of custody providers reduces institutional concerns about counterparty risk. Eased friction can encourage larger Bitcoin allocations and product innovation.
Why Regulatory Risk Has Been a Hidden Bitcoin Discount
Some institutions have avoided Bitcoin due to uncertainty around regulatory risks. Eased concerns could make the asset class more appealing to investment committees.
What Would Have to Happen for a New Institutional Wave to Begin?
The SEC needs workable custody rules, banks need viable economics, and ETF demand must persist. A favorable market environment will improve the chances for each.
The Risks: Why SEC Crypto Custody Reform Is Not Automatically Bullish
Custody Reform Does Not Guarantee New Bitcoin Demand
Improved infrastructure does not force institutions to purchase Bitcoin. They will still consider valuation, volatility, liquidity, and other factors.
Cybersecurity and Private-Key Risks Remain
Hacking, insider theft, software failures, and human error can lead to losses. Regulation cannot eliminate such technical and personnel risks.
Bank Capital Requirements Could Still Limit Adoption
SEC reforms will not eliminate every hindrance for banks. Capital requirements and other factors can impact their willingness to custody Bitcoin.
Regulatory Changes Could Be Reversed
Future administrations and courts can revisit crypto-related rules. Institutions will still seek stability and durability of rules over time.
Why Congress Still Matters
Acts of Congress can clarify agency mandates and reduce overall regulatory overlap. It can also help provide more durable rules than agencies alone.
SEC Crypto Custody Outlook: What Investors Should Watch Next
White House and OIRA Review
The White House represents the next critical custody inflection point. Regulatory agencies can request changes before the SEC proposes a rule.
The SEC’s Formal Proposed Rule
The actual SEC text will be critical in defining who qualifies as a custodian and which safeguards apply.
Public Comments and Industry Pushback
Banks, advisers, crypto firms, and investors will analyze the proposal in detail. Their comments will shape the final custody arrangement.
Final Custody Rules and Implementation Timeline
Rules may significantly differ from the initial proposal. Firms will also need time to update and implement new procedures.
The Next Catalyst for Institutional Bitcoin Adoption
New bank custody launches, continued ETF inflows, and reduced institutional friction can combine to support the next Bitcoin boom.
FAQ
What Is the SEC Crypto Custody?
SEC crypto custody refers to the ruleset concerning the crypto assets’ safekeeping. Therefore, this is the regulation of the SEC, covering the relevant aspects of custody, with particular emphasis on segregation, responsibility, and control.
What Are the SEC Crypto Custody Rules?
SEC crypto custody rules are the regulations concerning the custody practices in terms of advisers, brokers, and qualified custodians of record. These norms might directly impact the institutional Bitcoin market’s access.
What Did SAB 122 Change?
The main change in SEC crypto custody rules that SAB 122 introduced was eliminating an accounting SAB 121. This change likely creates more favorable conditions for banks to engage in custody compared to the SAB 121 environment.
Does Rule 15c3-3 Apply to Bitcoin?
According to SEC experts, Rule 15c3-3 does not concern Bitcoin. Indeed, the rule only applies to securities held in custody by a broker-dealer. Thus, for these cryptoassets, this provision is non-applicable.
Could SEC Crypto Custody Reform Drive Bitcoin Prices Higher?
Although the price driver is unproven, the custody reform indeed creates favorable conditions for institutional involvement in Bitcoin. Apart from this, this rule’s impact on Bitcoin investors is ambiguous; the reform cannot force prices higher merely based on regulations.
articles.summary:
The SEC is currently reviewing new, flexible crypto custody regulations that could remove significant barriers for banks and institutional investors looking to manage Bitcoin and other digital assets.

### Key Points
- The proposed initiative, currently under White House review as of August 2026, aims to replace restrictive, failed policies with a framework better suited for modern institutional adoption.
- Recent shifts, including the transition from SAB 121 to SAB 122, have already begun reducing the accounting and balance-sheet burdens that previously discouraged banks from offering custody services.
- New rules seek to clarify the roles of qualified custodians, potentially allowing traditional banks to compete directly with crypto-native firms for institutional business.
- Enhanced regulatory clarity is expected to lower counterparty risk and fees, potentially encouraging larger Bitcoin allocations from asset managers and family offices.
- Despite these reforms, technical risks like cybersecurity threats and potential future regulatory reversals remain significant factors for institutional investment committees.

### Why it Matters
Establishing a clear, workable custody framework is essential for integrating digital assets into the traditional financial system. By reducing operational and regulatory friction, these changes could unlock trillions in institutional capital and provide the infrastructure necessary for the next phase of Bitcoin market growth.

articles.title: Alpha Modus Stock Falls 29% After $200M Bitcoin Treasury Plan
articles.author: Editorial Staff
articles.content:
Alpha Modus Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: $AMOD $BTC
AMOD dropped about 29% to $2.72 in morning trading, giving the company an intraday market capitalization of roughly $18.9 million. The reaction put the scale of the proposed Bitcoin position in focus, with the assets being added worth more than ten times the company’s equity value at the time.
Alpha Modus said the transaction values Bitcoin at $71,000 per token. Under an agreement signed Aug. 26 with non-U.S. investors, the company would issue roughly 51.6 million Class A shares and warrants covering another 51.6 million shares in exchange for the 3,170 BTC.
More From Cryptoprowl:
Management expects the transaction to materially increase shareholder equity and help address an outstanding Nasdaq listing deficiency. The company said the Bitcoin addition would expand its asset base without changing its operating strategy across artificial intelligence, intellectual property and financial technology.
CEO William Alessi said Alpha Modus had considered a similar strategy when Bitcoin was near record highs but chose not to proceed. “We believed the better decision was to wait,” Alessi said, pointing to the current combination of asset value and balance-sheet impact.
The proposed deal comes as public-company Bitcoin treasury strategies face a tougher market backdrop. Alpha Modus is entering that trade with a digital asset position that would dwarf its existing market capitalization, while the share and warrant issuance creates a sizable potential dilution component for investors to weigh.
Completion still depends on the transaction closing, applicable accounting treatment and Nasdaq’s determination regarding continued listing compliance.

articles.title: 6 Windows 11 quality-of-life features you’ll wish you found sooner
articles.author: Pankil Shah
articles.content:
I’ve been using Windows 11 almost daily since launch, and I still sometimes find features I had no idea existed. And I’m not talking about anything that needs a registry hack to unlock. These are features that are either buried in menus or simply easy to miss. None of these are big enough to make a headline, but they can change the way you use your PC, or make the boring stuff a little less boring.
Use Winget to update all apps at once
A single command is all it takes
Windows gives you the freedom to download apps from wherever you want, but the only problem with that is keeping them all updated. Sure, Microsoft Store takes care of anything you’ve downloaded from it, but the rest of your apps still need to be updated manually.
Winget is a built-in package manager that can help you with this. All you have to do is open Command Prompt on your PC, type winget upgrade -all and hit Enter. It’ll scan every app installed on your PC, check for newer versions, and install them all in the background. You can also run the winget upgrade command to see what’s outdated before committing.
Winget isn’t just for app updates, either. It can also help you find, install, and remove apps with the same convenience.
Use the “End task” option to kill frozen apps
Skip the Task Manager
It’s never fun when an app freezes on you, but it can happen. The classic move in such cases is to open the Task Manager, find the process, right-click, and choose End task. It works, but there’s a quicker way to do this. Head to Settings > System > Advanced and enable the End Task toggle. Now, you can right-click any app on the taskbar and choose End task directly.
This isn’t just for closing frozen apps. I personally use this all the time when I’m done using an app and don’t want it running in the background. This frees up resources for other things and also improves battery life. Of course, this isn’t ideal for apps you need repeatedly. You should also avoid using it for apps that need to stay active in the background to save data or show notifications.
Use Windows Sandbox for the risky stuff
A disposable PC inside your main one
This one is only available for those using the Pro version of Windows 11. Windows Sandbox is a disposable PC that you can run inside your actual PC. It’s completely separate, and nothing you do inside can affect your personal files or security settings.
Sandbox essentially gives you the freedom to test unknown apps, open suspicious files, run scripts, and do basically anything you wouldn’t risk doing on your main PC. Once you close the Sandbox window, it deletes everything you’ve done, so there’s no trace left. When you reopen Sandbox, it loads a clean copy of Windows from scratch.
Mirror phone screen with Phone Link
The best Android emulator you're not using
For me, Phone Link’s best feature isn’t showing phone notifications or letting you make phone calls. It’s actually mirroring the phone screen on your PC because it gives you the freedom to interact with it while it’s charging or in your pocket.
Yes, using mobile apps with a mouse and keyboard can feel a bit awkward at first, but screen mirroring with Phone Link is honestly the best way to try Android apps on a PC. Its best feature is the new expanded view option, which lets apps use up to 90% of screen space. That means you’re not tied to that phone-shaped vertical layout anymore.
Customize touchpad gestures for productivity
You’ll want to ditch your mouse for good
Your laptop’s touchpad can do a lot more than click and scroll. Windows 11 is full of touchpad gestures that often get overlooked. You can use these to go forward and backward, switch apps, hide everything except the app in focus, control music playback, and even snap windows using Snap Layout.
The cherry on top is that none of it is locked in. Head to Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad and you can remap what three and four finger taps and swipes do. They might take a while getting used to, but they’re absolutely worth it.
Master keyboard shortcuts for these things
Use your PC like a pro
Much like touchpad gestures, keyboard shortcuts are nothing new, but there are a few that everyone should know about.
- Win + . opens an emoji panel over any app you’re using.
- Win + V opens a clipboard history that can remember everything you’ve copied recently.
- Win + Z lets you snap windows in a specific layout without hovering over the maximize button.
- Win + Ctrl + Shift lets you move apps between multiple monitors.
- Win + K lets you cast your PC’s screen to a TV or another display wirelessly.
Of course, this is all just the tip of the iceberg. Windows 11 has plenty of shortcuts like these that are worth memorizing.
articles.summary:
Windows 11 includes several hidden productivity features and built-in tools that allow users to streamline system maintenance, enhance security, and improve their overall workflow efficiency on the platform.

### Key Points
- Use the Winget package manager in Command Prompt with the command "winget upgrade --all" to automatically update all installed third-party applications.
- Enable the "End task" toggle in Settings to quickly close unresponsive or background applications directly from the taskbar without opening Task Manager.
- Windows 11 Pro users can utilize Windows Sandbox to create a secure, disposable virtual environment for testing suspicious files or unknown software.
- The Phone Link app enables Android screen mirroring on PCs, now supporting an expanded view that allows mobile apps to occupy more screen space.
- Users can customize touchpad gestures in Settings to improve navigation and utilize keyboard shortcuts like Win + V for clipboard history or Win + Z for window snapping.

### Why it Matters
These built-in tools reduce reliance on third-party software and help users optimize system performance and security without complex configurations. Mastering these features can significantly improve daily workflow efficiency and provide a more seamless experience for Windows 11 users.

articles.title: Apple Event Logo Hints at Two iPhone 18 Pro Features
articles.author: Tim Hardwick
articles.content:
Apple's logo for its upcoming September 9 "Surprise and shine" event hints at two rumored iPhone 18 Pro features, including new color options and a new camera system.
Apple fans often like to read into Apple's event invite graphics for clues about unreleased products, and this year Bloomberg's Mark Gurman is also taking part in the fun on Twitter (X).
First, Gurman says he sees the shining light behind Apple's logo as a nod to the "mechanical aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro Max."
MacRumors has been reporting since 2024 that Apple could introduce a variable aperture camera on the iPhone 18 Pro models – a first for any iPhone. However, a recent rumor out of China suggests the feature could be exclusive to the larger Pro Max model.
With a variable lens, the iPhone 18 Pro Max could allow users to manually shift the aperture, similar to on a DSLR camera. It could mean more control over depth of field and bright light, enabling sharper focus on subjects. That all depends on how Apple implements the feature, of course. It may be more automated than that.
Second, Gurman links the sky blue color of the event invite to a "possible new iPhone 18 Pro color." According to Macworld, Apple will likely introduce the device in Light Blue, alongside Dark Cherry (the new headline color), Dark Gray, and Silver.
What I am seeing: 
- Shining light = mechanical aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro Max
- Sky Blue color = Possible new iPhone 18 Pro color. https://t.co/MHQ21LmT9U
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) August 26, 2026
It's not like we have much longer to wait to find out whether these takes are correct. Apple's event is less than two weeks away. Stay tuned to MacRumors for all the last-minute details.
articles.summary:
Apple’s upcoming September 9 event invite suggests the iPhone 18 Pro series may feature a new mechanical aperture camera system and a fresh sky blue color option.

### Key Points
- Apple’s "Surprise and shine" event graphic hints at a variable aperture camera system for the iPhone 18 Pro Max.
- The rumored mechanical aperture would allow users to manually adjust depth of field, similar to professional DSLR camera functionality.
- Mark Gurman suggests the event's sky blue color scheme indicates a new aesthetic option for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro lineup.
- Additional rumored color variants for the new Pro models include Dark Cherry, Dark Gray, and Silver.
- The official product reveal is scheduled for Apple's September 9 event, which is less than two weeks away.

### Why it Matters
The introduction of a variable aperture would mark a significant hardware upgrade for iPhone photography, offering users greater control over focus and lighting conditions. This potential shift signals Apple's continued focus on competing with professional-grade camera equipment to maintain its premium market position.
